description: Dependency updates by the project's own bot: Renovate, run by the scheduled renovate job of .gitlab-ci.yml on linix (docs/ContinuousIntegration.md, 'Dependency updates').

Every datasource below is off GitHub: api.nuget.org, Microsoft's .NET release metadata, Docker Hub and mcr.microsoft.com, registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org, and the upstream projects' own release listings. hostRules refuses github.com, githubusercontent.com and ghcr.io outright, and fetchChangeLogs is off, because release notes are read from GitHub.
Nothing merges itself: there is no automerge anywhere in this file.

Every commit carries a Signed-off-by trailer naming its author, Renovate's git author (the :gitSignOff preset, built into Renovate): the sign-off job of .gitlab-ci.yml checks every commit of every merge request (CONTRIBUTING.md, 'Sign-off').

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A security fix goes to the newest fixed release (in the same major version where there is one), not the lowest. With two NuGet advisories on one package, Renovate 44.115 can choose the lower fix: the dry run proposed System.Text.Json 8.0.4 for advisories fixed in 8.0.4 and 8.0.5, which leaves the second open.

pip_requirements.description: The Python packages are chosen in the .in files and locked, with every dependency and the SHA-256 of every file PyPI has for each, in the .txt files uv makes from them (each file's header gives the command). Renovate reads the .in files only: its pip_requirements manager moves a version in a .txt file without resolving the others against it or hashing the new files, which on 28 September 2026 gave a merge request whose click 8.5.0 kept 8.4.2's hashes, and whose click, MCP, OpenTelemetry, jsonschema and PyJWT versions semgrep 1.178.0 does not accept (it asks for click~=8.4.2, mcp==1.29.0, opentelemetry-api~=1.37.0). The .txt files are in ignorePaths.

hostRules.description: The project takes nothing from GitHub (its account was suspended on 18 September 2026): no lookup, release note or digest is read from there.

Fedora's registry, and its CDN (cdn.registry.fedoraproject.org, a subdomain, which the registry redirects every blob to), one request at a time. Three daily runs in a row lost one Fedora lookup each, each time a different request and each time to a network error rather than an answer: on 28 and 29 September 2026 the tag list for .gitlab-ci.yml's fedora:44 ('no-result'), on 30 September the config blob of packages-rpm.yml's fedora:43 x86_64 pin, twice ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED ('Could not determine new digest' on the dashboard). The pins are right: Renovate reads a per-architecture pin's architecture from that blob and moves the pin to the same architecture's manifest of the tag's new index, and a lookup dry run the same evening resolved all seven Fedora pins of the tree. In the failing run Renovate logged seven requests to Fedora's registry in the 1.5 seconds before the failed one; one at a time is a mitigation, not a proven cure.

openssl.description: OpenSSL's own source page. Its links point at the release archives, which are hosted on GitHub; only the page on openssl-library.org is read, never an archive.

boost.description: Boost's release archive. The versions are written with underscores (1_92_0), the form the build's paths use.

postgresql.description: PostgreSQL's source directory: one v<major>.<minor>/ per release.

zlib.description: zlib's archive of every release, the current one included.

quickjs.description: Fabrice Bellard's QuickJS page, which links the newest release.

mariadb-connector-c.description: MariaDB's download API: every Connector/C release.

7-zip.description: 7-Zip's download page. The 'extra' package (7z<NNNN>-extra.7z) is the one 7za.exe comes from; its links point at GitHub, and only the page on 7-zip.org is read.

customManagers.description: NuGet packages of the three projects that still use packages.config (RegressionTests, StressTest, VMTestRunner.Console). Renovate's nuget manager reads PackageReference only. A version in packages.config is exact, but NuGet versioning reads a bare version as a minimum, and Renovate applies no rangeStrategy to a custom manager: every package looked current. So the version is handed to Renovate as NuGet's exact range, [x.y.z], and written back without the brackets.
OpenSSL, where the Windows build names it: the include and library paths of hMailServer.vcxproj, the installers' DLL paths, the post-build copy and build.ps1's copy of the ARM64 DLLs.
Boost, where the Windows build names it: the server's and the minidump tool's include and library paths, and the fuzz build's default.
The PostgreSQL client library (libpq), where the Windows build names it: hMailServer.vcxproj, the installers, the post-build copy and build.ps1's copy of the ARM64 DLLs.
zlib, vendored as source for COMPRESS=DEFLATE and the message store's compression: the version its own zlib.h declares.
QuickJS, vendored as source for the event scripts on Linux: the VERSION file its release ships, which CMake and the SBOM both read.
The MariaDB client (Connector/C) the Windows server loads for MySQL and MariaDB: its directory under libraries/, where the build, the test runner, git and the binary manifest name it.

Images named in a variable rather than on an image: line, which the gitlabci manager does not read: HM_COSIGN_IMAGE (.gitlab-ci.yml), the cosign every signing job runs in, HM_REGCTL_IMAGE (.gitlab/ci/channels.yml), the regctl the channels' jobs take out of its image, and scripts' defaults for them: HM_START_POSTGRES_IMAGE in build/ci/container-image-start-test.sh, which is container-image-start's PostgreSQL, and HM_SYSTEMD_UBUNTU_IMAGE and HM_SYSTEMD_FEDORA_IMAGE in build/ci/package-systemd-test.sh, the Ubuntu 26.04 and Fedora 44 images systemd runs in for package-systemd-ubuntu26.04 and package-systemd-fedora44. Each is written <image>:<tag>@sha256:<digest> and moves with the other container images, by the rules below: container-image.yml's regctl:<version>-alpine, which build/check-release-chain.py holds to HM_REGCTL_IMAGE's release, is read by the gitlabci manager and moves in the same merge request.
7-Zip's standalone console (7za.exe), which the installer carries: the build input the binary manifest names.

packageRules.description: NuGet in the SDK-style projects - the Control Panel, the tools, their tests and LinuxRegressionTests: one merge request a week. Renovate rewrites each project's packages.lock.json with 'dotnet restore --force-evaluate' on Linux, which for the net10.0-windows projects is not what Windows writes (the note says why), so the merge request is finished on Windows.
prBodyNotes: **Before merging, restore on Windows.** Renovate rewrote the lock files with a restore on Linux, and for the projects that target net10.0-windows a Linux restore lists packages the Windows Desktop runtime already carries (System.CodeDom under System.Management, System.Diagnostics.EventLog under System.ServiceProcess.ServiceController), which a restore on Windows leaves out: the dry run of 25 September 2026 showed it on master with the same SDK. On a Windows machine, on this branch, run `dotnet restore hmailserver/source/Tools/ControlPanel.sln --force-evaluate` and `dotnet restore "hmailserver/source/Tools/hMailServer Tools.sln" --force-evaluate`, and commit the lock files they rewrite (without --force-evaluate a restore that finds its project.assets.json current writes nothing). Otherwise the Windows gate's build rewrites them on the bench and leaves its checkout modified.

packageRules.description: global.json's SDK version is not proposed. With rollForward latestFeature it is the lowest .NET 10 SDK a build accepts, not the one it uses: every build already runs the newest 10.0 SDK installed on its machine. Raising it builds nothing differently and refuses every machine below it: on 30 September 2026 this laptop had 10.0.400, Alpine's dotnet10-sdk package, which the alpine-suite job runs the Linux suite with, is 10.0.303, and bench150 had 10.0.401, the version Renovate proposed on 28 September. It is raised by hand when a build needs a newer SDK; Microsoft's SDK image, which the Linux jobs take theirs from, keeps moving with its digest.

Placeholder for the .NET runtime the installer bundles. build/get-dotnet-runtime.ps1 takes the newest 10.0 from aka.ms by channel today, so there is no pin to update. When the supply-chain row pins it to an exact version, add a customManager for that line with datasourceTemplate dotnet-version and depNameTemplate dotnet-runtime; this rule then puts it in the NuGet merge request, and the rule below keeps it on .NET 10.

The .NET major version moves by hand, in one commit: global.json, every TargetFramework, DOTNET_MAJOR in hMailServer64.iss and the SDK image of build/ci/linux.Dockerfile (global.json's own comment says so).

The packages.config projects. Visual Studio's package manager changes three things together - packages.config, the HintPath and Import paths in the .csproj and the assembly version in each Reference - and Renovate can change only the first. So a routine update waits on the dependency dashboard, and a merge request, when one is opened, is a notice. One proposal per package, the newest stable release: a security fix for these packages is placed after Renovate's version lookup, so it takes the first proposal there is, and with the patch release kept apart that was 12.0.3 for an advisory fixed in 13.0.1.
packageRules.groupName: NuGet packages of the packages.config projects
prBodyNotes: **This merge request is a notice; do not merge it as it is.** {{{packageFile}}} belongs to a project that uses packages.config, and Renovate changed that file alone. Update the package in Visual Studio (Manage NuGet Packages for Solution, Updates) on a branch of your own: that rewrites packages.config, the HintPath and Import paths and the assembly versions in the .csproj together. Then close this merge request.

packageRules.description: Container images - the Dockerfiles, .gitlab-ci.yml's images and services, and the packaging compose file - from Docker Hub and mcr.microsoft.com: one merge request a week, and each image pinned by digest.
Microsoft's .NET SDK image stays on .NET 10: the .NET major version moves by hand, with every TargetFramework (the dotnet-version rule above). Its digest moves weekly.

A distribution's own image names a release, and a new release is a change made by hand, so only each tag's digest moves. Most name a release a package is built for or installed on (Debian 12 and 13, Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04, Fedora 43 and 44, UBI 9 and 10, openSUSE Leap 16.0 and Tumbleweed, AlmaLinux 10 and Alpine 3.24: .gitlab/ci/packages-*.yml, source-packages.yml, alpine.yml and .gitlab-ci.yml's linux-package-* jobs), where a new release is a new target with jobs of its own and moving the tag would drop the target it names. The Linux CI image's Ubuntu is the one linux-build makes the .deb and the .rpm in, and the container image's Ubuntu the release its .deb was built on (its Dockerfile says why). The rest run a tool from the release's own packages (editorconfig, chart-and-compose, update-helper, package-repos, ppa-upload, helm-chart-package, several pinning a package job's image on purpose), where a new release is a new version of the tool. On 30 September 2026 the dashboard offered Debian 12 to 13, Ubuntu 24.04 to 26.04, Fedora 43 and 44 to 46 (Rawhide in Fedora's registry that day) and openSUSE Leap 16.0 to 16.1 and to 42.3, the 2017 release, which Renovate's versioning ranks above 16.

The test lab (build/lab/docker-compose.yml): its matrix - MySQL 8.4, MariaDB 11.8 LTS, PostgreSQL 17, SQL Server 2022 and the peers it tests against - is chosen, and docs/TestLab.md's results are for those versions. A new version there is a new run of the matrix, made by hand; only the digests move.

The databases the CI jobs test against - PostgreSQL 18 for the Linux suite, the upgrade gates and the package, live-update and container start tests, MariaDB 13 for the MySQL upgrade gate - and the packaging compose file's PostgreSQL, which is what users deploy: a PostgreSQL major version does not open the data directory of the one before, so a new one there is a move of each deployment's hm-db volume, as 16 to 18 was (docs/ContainerImage.md, Updates). And GitLab's security analyzers, where a file names one on GitLab's registry: semgrep-sast is one of the four scans the release job reads (build/ci/security-gate.py), with its accepted findings in .gitlab/security-exceptions.yml, and an analyzer's major version changes its rules and so its findings. Each stays on its major version, and its digest moves; a new major version is a decision and a run, made by hand by changing this rule. semgrep-sast and secret_detection run the project's copies of them instead (the rule below).

cosign stays on its major version, 2: the release scripts were written for cosign 2, and cosign 3 follows Sigstore's signing configuration, which can send a signature to Rekor v2 with another key and no integratedTime, which no server built after 6.3.3 reads (build/ci/release-sign.sh says so). Its digest moves; a new major version is a decision and a run of the release chain, made by hand by changing this rule.

Images that are not looked up: the project's own - registry.gitlab.com/hmailserver/hmailserver, which the Compose file and the chart name and each release pushes from its own pipeline (a digest pinned here would be a release older than the file), registry.gitlab.com/progressiverobot/hmailserver, the project's path before its move, where no image is pushed, and ghcr.io/progressiverobot/hmailserver, its name until GitHub suspended the account (GitHub is refused anyway); the Tumbleweed snapshot mirrored at registry.gitlab.com/hmailserver/hmailserver/mirror/opensuse-tumbleweed, which build/ci/mirror-tumbleweed.sh refreshes by hand because openSUSE's registry drops a rolling snapshot within weeks (packages-rpm.yml says why); GitLab's semgrep and secrets analyzers as semgrep-sast and secret_detection run them, registry.gitlab.com/hmailserver/hmailserver/mirror/semgrep and mirror/secrets, which build/ci/mirror-semgrep.sh and build/ci/mirror-secrets.sh copy by hand, digest preserved, because GitLab's registry stops serving a digest its tag has moved on from (.gitlab/ci/gitlab-security.yml says why); and the Linux CI image, registry.gitlab.com/hmailserver/hmailserver/ci-linux, which is built on linix from build/ci/linux.Dockerfile and pushed by hand (build/ci/build-linux-image.sh --push), under a tag made from the Dockerfile's own hash that build/check-ci-image.py holds .gitlab-ci.yml to, so it moves only with the Dockerfile.
An edit to build/ci/linux.Dockerfile is a new image tag.
prBodyNotes: **build/ci/linux.Dockerfile changed, so the Linux jobs' image tag changes.** On this branch, put the tag `python build/check-ci-image.py` prints into .gitlab-ci.yml (the checkers job fails until then), and build the image on linix with `bash build/ci/build-linux-image.sh` before the pipeline for the merged commit reaches it (docs/ContinuousIntegration.md, 'The image').

packageRules.description: npm: no package.json in the tree today (the harnesses use Node's standard library only). One added later is covered, one merge request a week.
Python: the .in files of build/ and build/ci/ and the command-line package's pyproject.toml, one merge request a week.
prBodyNotes: **Remake the locked .txt file of each .in file this merge request changes, on this branch.** Renovate changed the chosen versions only. Run the uv command in the .txt file's header, in the image its job runs in (the .in file says which), which resolves every dependency against the new versions and hashes every file PyPI has for them; a version the others do not accept fails there, not in the pipeline. For build/ci/requirements.in, run build/ci/semgrep.sh and regenerate its baseline if the new Semgrep finds what the old one did not (docs/ContinuousIntegration.md, 'Security scanning').

packageRules.description: A new release waits three days before it is proposed, so that a release pulled soon after it was published is never offered. Security fixes do not wait.
The native libraries the Windows build compiles against, built from source on each build machine by libraries/build-*.ps1: one merge request a week.
prBodyNotes: **A native library: this merge request changes the build's paths, and the build needs the library built first.** On every Windows build machine and the bench, build {{{depName}}} {{{newVersion}}} with its script (libraries/build-openssl.ps1, build-boost.ps1 with the version in dots, build-pgsql.ps1), passing -Sha256 the digest published beside the release (OpenSSL's script takes the archive from Debian's archive, openssl_<version>.orig.tar.gz, since OpenSSL publishes its releases only on GitHub, which the project does not download from; until Debian carries the new version, pass -Archive with a copy obtained by hand), and add that digest to the script's digest table on this branch. Then change the version where the documents name it (`git grep` the old one: README.md, hmailserver/docs) and run `python build/generate-help-pages.py`. The Linux build uses the distribution's packages and is not affected.

packageRules.description: An OpenSSL patch release fixes security advisories as a rule, so it comes on any day, in a merge request of its own, instead of waiting for Monday's native-libraries group. Renovate's advisory alerts do not reach the custom datasources: OpenSSL 4.0.3, published on 29 September 2026 with thirteen advisories against 4.0.2, which the Windows installers ship, reached the dashboard as a routine update for the next Monday. The native libraries' note (above) still applies.
The C++ libraries stay on their major version. A major upgrade is a decision, not a weekly bump: change this rule by hand to take one.

Vendored source and fetched binaries: a new release is listed on the dependency dashboard and waits there, because the upgrade is a new copy of the source or a new build input, which Renovate cannot make.
prBodyNotes: **This merge request is a notice; do not merge it as it is.** Renovate changed the version string of {{{depName}}}, not what the build uses. zlib and QuickJS are vendored as source (hmailserver/source/Server/zlib, hmailserver/source/Server/quickjs): replace the sources with the release's. The MariaDB client and 7za.exe are build inputs (hmailserver/docs/third-party-binaries.json, build/get-installer-binaries.ps1): publish the new files as a build-inputs release and record their hashes. Then close this merge request.
